text:
Meera (sales): FYI - partner NovaHealth reporting p95 latency up ~2x and throughput down ~20% since last Wednesday. Sales pushed for priority review, customer in PROD. Link to support ticket: https://support.redwood.example/ticket/CH-7732
Liam (support): Confirmed. They saw spikes after the 2026-03-10 runtime deploy, around 03:12 UTC. I've attached sample request IDs and a short trace.
Alex (oncall): Thanks Meera. Can you paste the sample request IDs and which model/route they use? Also any dedicated vs hosted info?
Meera (sales): Route is /v1/generate, model beefy-open-7b-quant, hosted (standard account), customer not on dedicated. Sample IDs: req_9a1f, req_9a2b, req_9a7c. Latency p95 ~820ms -> ~1700ms.
Javier (eng-runtime): Noted. 7b quant recently got a kernel patch in that deploy. I'll check kernel selection logs and batching behavior. Repro plan: run traffic-replay for the request IDs, compare before/after kernels.
Alex (oncall): Oncall-bot: start trace capture for NovaHealth org id 2244 for next 6 hours.
oncall-bot: Trace capture started (id tc-2244-194567).
Javier (eng-runtime): Quick check of metrics shows sustained increase in queue_time at the front of the runtime for that model around the deploy window. Could be batching config or a change in KV cache sharding.
Priya (product): Sales is asking for prioritization into the product backlog for a possible rollback or mitigation. What's our triage outcome threshold for prioritizing a customer-impacting perf regression?
Alex (oncall): For customer-facing regressions hitting prod p95 > 1.5x and SLA risk we escalate to P2 and product should triage for backlog priority. This meets that.
Priya (product): Understood. We'll need RCA notes, repro steps, and a customer-facing mitigation plan before prioritizing work into the roadmap. If it's a runtime kernel bug, eng-runtime will need a patch + canary and targeted rollback plan.
Javier (eng-runtime): I'll attempt to repro with traffic-replay and a canary on a dev pool. If repro is consistent, plan: 1) hotfix to revert kernel change 2) canary deploy to 10% 3) full rollback if passes. ETA for first repro attempt: 2h.
Liam (support): Customer is asking for a temporary workaround — any config tweaks we can surface quickly (e.g., reduce max_batch_size or change batching window)?
Javier (eng-runtime): Short-term: reducing max_batch_size to 8 or setting batch_timeout lower (6ms) may reduce queueing and p95, but may increase cost. I can prepare a small runbook for support to push a config change on their API route.
Meera (sales): Customer prefers a temporary config change while you investigate. They'll accept possible cost delta if it stabilizes latency.
Priya (product): OK let's capture as follows: backlog item 'novahealth p95 regression' with labels customer:priority, severity:P2, owner:eng-runtime. Product will convert to an RFC only if hotfix isn't straightforward. For now, treat as operational incident with a mitigation path.
Alex (oncall): Assigning oncall owner Javier. Javier, please post updates in this thread every 30-60 mins or when you hit a milestone. Also include exact repro command and any logs we can share with product/support.
Javier (eng-runtime): Will do. First update: I kicked off traffic-replay against the current runtime; early signals show increased kv_cache_miss rate and larger batch sizes than before. Capturing kernel selection logs now.
Meera (sales): Noted — forwarding the customer's willingness to accept config change. I'll be on standby for communications.
Liam (support): I'll prepare the runbook to toggle max_batch_size and batch_timeout and share it here. If we can get a config patch out in the next hour that's ideal.
Priya (product): Thanks. Once we have repro steps + mitigation, product will decide if this becomes an engineering initiative or stays incident-driven. Please add estimated dev effort in the next update.
Alex (oncall): Good. Oncall-bot: create incident ticket INC-2026-0331-novahealth and link this thread.
oncall-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-0331-novahealth created (severity P2).
Javier (eng-runtime): Update 45m: repro confirmed in dev pool, root cause points to a kernel path that increases copying for quantized KV lookups under certain sequence lengths. Preparing a minimal rollback to previous kernel (patch branch: fix/quant-kv-copy-rollback).
Meera (sales): Thanks — customer says they need ETA for fix or rollback. Any rough timeline?
Javier (eng-runtime): If rollback passes canary, ~3-4 hours to full rollback and monitor. Will update.
Priya (product): I'll slot a short cross-functional checkpoint once you have canary results. If rollback looks risky we'll scope surface-level mitigations into a short ticket for next sprint.
Alex (oncall): Thanks everyone. Keep updates here.
